chapter: Bix after Whiteman and his piano pieces
title: Bix's piano pieces sound alike; transcribing Davenport Blues
summary: He explains the family resemblance of Bix's pieces and how he wrote Davenport Blues from a record after Bix's death.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you something a propos of Bix's -- in listening, you know, to the whole set of pieces, you know, not so much Davenport Blues but, you know, "Flashes," "Candlelight," "In the Dark" and -- there is -- there are certain similarities from piece to piece and certain things were -- makes them sound very much, almost of one.
Yeah, out of the same mold.
Yeah, well, this is what -- this is what -- well, I think he could have gotten over it. Now, "Davenport Blues" was done way back.
I had to get that. I was given a record to take it off, and then I had to put in the introduction and the ending and make it like it would conform to what Bix was doing.
So he was putting on his introduction, and he was putting on his endings; you know, he'd always have that slow part, beautiful part. He'd go out with some nice
chords and so forth. So I did that on Davenport." Now, that's over with. That was done after his death.
